hooks: You have a plan. Where do you spend limited time first: what could hurt most?
Risks are ranked. How do you turn them into a small set of sharp test cases?
Scripted cases miss surprises. What does a skilled tester find just by exploring?
Exploring finds new problems. Which repeated checks should a machine run instead?
Automation is only useful when it runs. Where in the pipeline should it fire?
Bugs will still turn up. How is one tracked from report to closed?
Lots of bugs, little time. Who decides which to fix now?
Triage works. How do you know the whole process is actually improving?
test-strategy.upNext: Next, UI Automation: turning the repeated checks into reliable browser tests.

hooks: You picked a tool. How does a test find the right button without breaking next sprint?
You found the element. Is it ready yet, and how long should the test wait?
Waits are fixed, yet some tests still fail at random. What causes flakes?
Flakes under control. How do you keep selectors out of every test file?
Tests are tidy. How do you run hundreds quickly in CI with their own data?
Passing is not the same as looking right. How do you catch layout bugs and browser differences?
selenium-playwright.upNext: Next, API Testing: faster, steadier checks one layer below the browser.

hooks: You have a tool. What exactly should you check in a response?
The body is right. What about status headers, content types and metadata?
Many endpoints need a login. How do tests get and reuse valid tokens?
You are signed in. What data should the test start with, and who cleans it up?
Happy paths pass. What should happen when the input is wrong or missing?
Bad input is handled. What about callers who try to reach data they should not see?
Some dependencies are slow or unavailable. How do you stand in for them?
Mocks can drift from the real service. How do two teams prove they still agree?
api-testing.upNext: Next, Performance Testing: how the API behaves with thousands of callers instead of one.

hooks: With a goal, which kind of test fits: load, stress, spike or soak?
You know the test types. What should the traffic actually look like?
A good model needs a place to run. How close to production must it be?
The environment is ready. Which tool will generate the load?
Load is running. How do you read p95, throughput and error rate without being fooled?
The numbers look bad. How do you find where the time actually goes?
The bottleneck is a resource. When does adding more help, and when does a limit stop it?
You can fix it once. How do you stop it getting slow again next release?
performance-testing.upNext: Next, Application Security: finding the flaws that load and functional tests never catch.

hooks: That is the map of risks. Start with the classic: what happens when user input becomes code?
Input is safe. What stops one user reading another user's record by changing an ID?
Access is checked per request. How do you know who is asking and keep sessions safe?
Login holds. Where do API keys and passwords live so they never reach the repo?
Practices are set. How do you catch mistakes automatically on every commit?
Scanners miss logic flaws. What should a human look for in a code review?
appsec.upNext: Next, Threat Modeling: finding design flaws before any code exists to scan.

hooks: You know what threat modeling is. When in a project should you actually do it?
Early and often. What do you draw first?
You have a diagram. Where does trust change between its parts?
Boundaries are marked. How do you ask what can go wrong at each one?
You have a list of threats. How do you decide which matter most?
Ranked threats need action. How do you track each fix to done?
Tracking needs a plan. What options do you have for dealing with each threat?
You have the full method. Try it on something real: a typical web app.
threat-modeling.upNext: Next, Behavioral: how to tell the story of what you have built and learned.
